question.leadin: This woman took the name Rebecca after converting to Christianity and later married John Rolfe.
question.text: In a heavily embellished account, John Smith credited what daughter of Chief Powhatan with saving him from an execution?
question.clue: Thomas Dale held this figure captive in Henricus following her abduction by Samuel Argall.

swap.leadin: Name these New World Colonies now known by their state names.
swap.text: Captain John Smith helped to found Jamestown, a settlement within this colony.
swap.clue: A deputy governor of this colony issued 81 draconian provisions called Dale's Laws.

question.text: In this 1676 war, which included the Great Swamp Fight, a namesake chief fought soldiers and priests from Plymouth and Massachusetts Bay. Native or colonial name acceptable.
question.answerHtml: King Philip’s War [or Metacomet’s War; or Pometacomet’s War; accept “rebellion” in place of “war”]
question.clue: A turning point in this conflict occurred with the Great Swamp Fight, after which the Narragansett were forced to withdraw.

swap.leadin: Give the following about labor practices in 19th century America.
swap.text: Many Europeans migrated to the Americas by becoming this type of laborer, in which they exchanged several years of labor for their passage and were guaranteed their freedom at the end of the contract.
swap.answerHtml: indentured servants (accept word forms, like indentured servitude; prompt on servant)
swap.clue: The book's second chapter argues that the "color line" was created to pacify these people by distinguishing them from slaves. These servants worked without pay for a set amount of time.

question.text: This body was the elected portion of the Virginia General Assembly, the legislative body of colonial Virginia.
question.clue: Distinguished members included Captain Francis West and Reverend William Wickham.

swap.leadin: This rebellion opposed the favoritism given to the Green Spring Faction.
swap.text: Name this 1676 rebellion in colonial Virginia against governor William Berkeley. Its namesake organized discontented indentured servants before dying of dysentery.
swap.clue: A target of this conflict who owned the Green Spring Plantation was William Berkeley.

question.leadin: Sassacus led one side in this war.
question.text: Name this war, during which colonists under John Mason killed hundreds of Narragansetts during the Mystic Massacre.
question.clue: The Mohawks effectively ended this war after they killed the Grand Sachem Sassacus as a sign of goodwill to the English colonists.

swap.leadin: Identify these things about the English colonies in America.
swap.text: Pontiac's rebellion led to this British law forbidding colonists from moving past the Appalachian mountains because they were afraid of wars with Indians draining resources.
swap.clue: This law was modified within five years by the treaties of Hard Labor and Lochaber.

question.leadin: This man's son of the same name helped unite the colony of Connecticut and he himself delivered a sermon on "A Model of Christian Charity", likening his colony to "a City upon a Hill."
question.text: Name this man who succeeded John Endecott in 1630, a frequent governor of the Massachusetts Bay Colony.
question.clue: He sided with Thomas Dudley and John Endecott in a dispute that led to the banishment of John Wheelwright.

swap.leadin: Identify these people whose names are associated with civil liberties, or the denial thereof.
swap.text: He published the New York Weekly Journal, which criticized governor William Cosby. His acquittal in a 1735 libel case helped establish the free press in America.
swap.clue: During his trial, the judge declared that the jury would be perjured if they found him not guilty.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Poor Richard's Almanack.
question.text: Benjamin Franklin, who wrote Poor Richard's Almanack, had earlier written in the New England Courant under this pseudonym. 14 letters published in 1722 were attributed to Franklin under this pseudonym.
question.clue: As an apprentice, Benjamin Franklin printed the New-England Courant newspaper, which featured this female persona of his giving humorous accounts of colonial life.

swap.leadin: The namesakes of this land survey were hired to settle a dispute between Maryland and Pennsylvania.
swap.text: What pair of British astronomers created a namesake line that demarcates four states?
swap.clue: They fulfilled the task by laying out a series of milestones bearing coats of arms until trouble with natives forced a return to Philadelphia.

question.text: The Fundamental Agreement of the New Haven Colony created a court of 16 people with this title, who were "chosen out of the church members." Elected representatives in colonial Virginia also had this title.

swap.leadin: This tribe developed a voting procedure where a corn kernel meant agreement, while a pea meant opposition.
swap.text: Name this matrilineal tribe that signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation with the English. This tribe's Queen Cockacoeske was succeeded by Queens Betty and Ann, who may have been the same person.
swap.clue: This tribe's female chief Cockacoeske was killed during Bacon's Rebellion. Powhatan and his daughter Pocahontas belonged to this tribe.

question.leadin: This insurrection was spurned by attempts to enforce the Navigation Acts and the Plantation Duty Act.
question.text: Name this insurrection that led to the establishment of a largely independent government for two years in Albemarle County.
question.clue: This 1677 rebellion in the Albemarle region, in which settlers overthrew the colonial government in protest of the enforcement of the Navigation Acts.

swap.leadin: Robert Fogel posited one of these periods spanning roughly the 1960s through 80s, though William G. McLoughlin's thesis about the third period of this type is much more widely accepted.
swap.text: Name these periods of spiritual revival in America, whose first iteration was exemplified by Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield.
swap.answerHtml: Great Awakenings [accept First, Second, Third, or Fourth Great Awakening]
swap.clue: In 1801, over 20,000 people participated in one of these events by attending the Cane Ridge Revival in Kentucky.

question.leadin: This association created a five-member court to run its territory chaired by John Carter, and negotiated with Cherokee Indians to make the Transylvania Purchase.
question.text: Name this association which, in 1772, established an autonomous republic on the banks of the namesake river in Tennessee when they realized they were living south of the official territory of North Carolina.

swap.leadin: Identify these preachers active during the Great Awakening FTPE.
swap.text: This priest of Boston's First Church was the staunchest opponent of the Great Awakening and warned against believing itinerant preachers. His most famous sermon was Enthusiasm Described and Cautioned Against.
swap.clue: Both Whitefield and Edwards were attacked by this Boston divine, whose 1742 sermon Enthusiasm Described and Cautioned Against saw in the Awakening the legacy of the Munster Anabaptists and Antinomians.

question.text: This governor tried to regulate trade with tribes south of the James River, particularly the Saponi and Tutelo, in 1714 by creating Fort Christanna and the Virginia Indian Company, but William Byrd saw this quashed by the Lords of Trade in 1718.
question.clue: This royal governor of colonial Virginia sent the Knights of the Golden Horseshoe, a 1716 expedition to the Blue Ridge Mountains. He also set up the mining settlement Germanna for, you guessed it, German immigrants.

swap.text: Wampum and beaver pelts were the currency of this colony. This colony was the site of Keift's War and was led by Pieter Stuyvesant for a long time.
swap.clue: This colony which fought with the Algonquin in the Peach Tree War while being led by a man with a pegleg.
